> period (yet has a plus):
>
> Please just let me know which characters you would like to allow. No MR needed.

By looking into the history of r-base (which provides the virtual
r-api-xx package), we have: r-api-3, r-api-3.4, r-api-3.5 and

now. I think it would be fine if lintian could detect both formats
r-api-X and r-api-X.X where X is numeric.

Thanks again!

Best,
Dylan

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dylan,

On Wed, Jul 8, 2020 at 10:45 PM Dylan Aïssi <daissi at debian.org> wrote:
>
> it would be fine if lintian could detect both formats
> r-api-X and r-api-X.X where X is numeric.

To give your teams the greatest possible flexibility I allowed in the
extension all characters that are legal for package names. API version
numbers that are carried into the package names may now also contain
plus and minus (as well as the entire alphabet). From my experience,
the prefix 'r-api-' will ensure that it works the way you expect.

    https://salsa.debian.org/lintian/lintian/-/commit/c4a141e83625b3d424bcf3d31f575aab4c1c2fa0

Please write again if something does not work, after all (or stops
working). Please also feel free to contribute additional tags for R or
any of your other products.

Kind regards
Felix Lechner

messages.subject: How about a metapackage for pulling frequent build and check dependencies ?
messages.subject_clean: How about a metapackage for pulling frequent build and check dependencies ?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Dirk and everybody,

sometimes I need to create a Debian container in which I will install
all the CRAN and Bioconductor packages that I need from source.

I often end up installing libxml2-dev, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libssl-dev,
and texlive by hand.  And each time, it takes me a minute of distraction
in order to find the name of the package to install.

I wonder if it would be useful to have a "r-suggested" or "r-extra"
metapackage in Debian that would depend on them.

Have a nice day,

Charles

-- 
Charles Plessy                              Akano, Uruma, Okinawa, Japan
Debian Med packaging team         http://www.debian.org/devel/debian-med
Tooting from work,           https://mastodon.technology/@charles_plessy
Tooting from home,                 https://framapiaf.org/@charles_plessy

messages.body_plain:
Salut Charles,

On 10 July 2020 at 11:06, Charles Plessy wrote:
| Hello Dirk and everybody,
| 
| sometimes I need to create a Debian container in which I will install
| all the CRAN and Bioconductor packages that I need from source.

There are existing solutions that look at a package (in the CRAN/BioC sense)
and bundle all it needs into a container. I keep forgetting the names but they
are mentioned in the paper by Daniel Nuest (with me and a lots of others):
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.10641

| I often end up installing libxml2-dev, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libssl-dev,
| and texlive by hand.  And each time, it takes me a minute of distraction
| in order to find the name of the package to install.
| 
| I wonder if it would be useful to have a "r-suggested" or "r-extra"
| metapackage in Debian that would depend on them.

On just those four? Maybe.

Maybe we could even add them to r-base-dev, come to think about it. Or, as
you say, make a 'r-base-extra-dev'. (Or, as I sometimes do for pragmatic
reasons, you use Ubuntu with the Rutter PPAs giving you ~ 4500 r-cran-*
binaries that just work. May be the better approach actually...)

And there is another issue with those four and some others. RStudio now
offers binaries for "everything" incl four Linux distros (but Debian, very
strange) and those are "just binary CRAN installs" i.e. NOT package in our
sense with a dependency graph. So ... sometimes you will miss depends. I
blogged a little about it and have two test containers (for Ubuntu 18.04 and
20.04 if you want to play). Blog post is at
  https://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/2020/07/03/#028_rocker_rspm

Bye, Dirk

-- 
https://dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org

messages.body_plain:
Hi Shayan,

On Thu, Jul 16, 2020 at 01:52:55AM +0100, Shayan Doust wrote:
> A more of an introductory email after joining this team. My name is
> Shayan Doust, and for the past few months, have been packaging for the
> Debian Med team.

:-)
 
> I've decided to join this team alongside with what I have been doing in
> Debian so far as I am currently learning R. As well as introducing new
> packages which I am using (some of which are not yet available as a
> package), It'd be great to offer a helping hand. Not forgetting that
> this will be a great learning experience for handling anything R-related :).

I think the most interesting fact to learn is that you never should
start packaging something manually.  Just use

   prepare_missing_cran_package CRANNAME

from dh-r package and check the dir

   ../CRAN_prospective

afterwards.  It should contain a git repository with your target package
(and all its dependencies).  If you want more details I'd recommend one
of the two "R packaging BOF" videos you can find here

   https://people.debian.org/~tille/talks/

Welcome in the team

       Andreas.

--
